CANONICAL SOP (reify) — landing PRD artifacts (PRD .md, capability-manifest .md, YAML sidecar). RE-ISSUED 2026-07-27 under human curator gate esc-5541-1 (reify task 5541). This entry REPLACES retired uuid 166f5106-00da-4364-9c6f-d0a0d514db7a and every earlier reify PRD-landing procedure; 14 pre-canonical entries were deleted at this gate (see the docs-prd-landing closure record filed alongside this entry). Mem0 uuids churn on consolidation — cite this by topic (`topic='docs-prd-landing'`), never by uuid.

DURABLE CARRIER: this SOP is also codified in the repo at `.claude/skills/prd/project.md` §"Landing PRD artifacts" and `CLAUDE.md` §"Landing on main". Those are always in context and are authoritative if this entry ever drifts from them.

RULE: commit PRD artifacts DIRECTLY ON main in project_root (/home/leo/src/reify). Do NOT route docs through the orchestrator merge queue, and do NOT use scripts/land.sh.

ARTIFACT SCOPE — `.ri` FIXTURES ARE EXCLUDED (carve-out in force while reify task 5536 is open; re-check 5536's live status before relying on it). `decide_scope` (scripts/verify.sh:1027) fast-paths only `docs/*|*.md|*.yaml|*.yml`. `tests/prd-gate/fixtures/*.ri` falls through to the `*)` default (:1030) → `rust=1; gui=1; gate=1`, i.e. the FULL ~20k-test workspace nextest plus the OCCT gate (45+ min, load-flaky, serialized on the shared index.lock; observed twice on 2026-07-25). So: land PRD .md + capability-manifest .md + YAML sidecar docs-only in the single commit, and deliver `.ri` gate fixtures in the grammar/implementation task's own diff. IMPORTANT REFINEMENT: only STAGED `.ri` files escalate the gate — untracked `.ri` sitting in the working tree do not, because the gate scopes by `git diff --cached`.

WHY (both branch paths are the SLOW ones): reify's merge gate stamps DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge, which makes scripts/verify.sh force --scope all (contract C2, verify.sh:778) and --profile both (verify.sh:602); dark-factory's INV-1 additionally REFUSES the docs-only trivial pass at merge role and escalates it to the full global gate, because an adoptable merge verdict must never be stamped from zero evidence (verify.py:5319 and :5497 — `if not _has_source_files(...)` then `if role == 'merge' and is_merge_verify:` → escalate or fail loud). So a docs-only merge costs the same cold debug+release workspace build as landing a compiler change (reify budgets merge_verify_cold_command_timeout_secs: 10800 = 3h). scripts/land.sh is equally expensive — its pre-merge-commit hook runs `DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge verify.sh all --profile both --scope all`. The pre-2026-07-06 belief that "docs changes hit the merge worker's trivial-pass and land in seconds" was true when written and is FALSE now; it was independently re-falsified by direct observation four times (2026-06-18 x2, 07-24, 07-25). By contrast a plain commit on main runs hooks/pre-commit -> `verify.sh all --profile debug --scope staged --include-infra` with DF_VERIFY_ROLE unset (role 'task', so no C2 force), and decide_scope classifies docs as no-heavy-checks: seconds.

IT IS SANCTIONED, NOT A VIOLATION: hooks/pre-commit runs project-checks on main and then calls main_gate_mark, so hooks/reference-transaction logs the ref move as SANCTIONED. The CLAUDE.md main-gate invariant forbids moving main WITHOUT a gate (merge --no-verify / update-ref / reset / commit-tree plumbing) — a hook-gated commit on main is not that.

SEQUENCE:
1. Write the artifacts as untracked files in project_root at their canonical paths (PRD docs/prds/<vM_N>/<slug>.md, manifest <slug>.capability-manifest.md, sidecar <slug>.capability-manifest.yaml).
2. File the batch with planning_mode=True, wire deps, then commit_planning — it stamps the on-disk sidecar IN PLACE and copies delivered_checks into producer metadata. Flip FIRST, commit the STAMPED sidecar once; never land an unstamped sidecar and stamp afterwards.
3. `git add <each exact file path>` — never `git add -A` and never a directory. project_root is a shared hot checkout with concurrent /prd sessions and the orchestrator; a directory add sweeps foreign untracked files into your commit.
4. `git commit --only <same exact paths> -F <msgfile>` — `--only`/`-o` with an explicit pathspec ignores foreign staged state. (A pathspec commit alone fails on untracked files, which is why step 3 exists.) If you use the `--` pathspec-separator form, `-F <msgfile>` MUST come BEFORE the `--`, else git parses the message-file path as a pathspec and fails with "outside repository": `git commit --only -F <msgfile> -- <paths>`, never `git commit --only -- <paths> -F <msgfile>`.

ORDERING HAZARD (recovered from the retired 2026-05-27 procedure): `commit_planning` in step 2 flips the batch to `pending`, i.e. schedulable — so between step 2 and step 4 the tasks are dispatchable while their PRD is not yet on main, and a worker branching from main gets a worktree without its own spec. Keep steps 2->4 back-to-back; do not file the batch, walk away, and commit later. If the window cannot be kept short, flip the batch AFTER the commit instead, accepting that the sidecar must then be re-stamped.

HARD TRAPS:
- NEVER `--no-verify` on main. `reify.mainGate.enforce` is true; --no-verify skips pre-commit, so no sentinel is marked, hooks/reference-transaction sees an UNSANCTIONED main move and HARD-ABORTS the transaction. (This is dark-factory's docs-only-commit habit; it is fatal in reify.)
  - NARROW EXCEPTION — `REIFY_MAIN_GATE_BYPASS=1` is a code-recognized BREAK-GLASS, not a fast path. hooks/reference-transaction:82 evaluates `main_gate_bypass_on` BEFORE both the non-fast-forward guard and the sentinel check, and unconditionally allows + logs the move as `bypass main move` (sources: env REIFY_MAIN_GATE_BYPASS, `git config reify.mainGate.bypass`, or the flag file — hooks/main-gate-lib.sh:67-79). It only stops the REF MOVE aborting; --no-verify still skips pre-commit, so no gate ran and no sentinel was marked, and what lands on main is UNVERIFIED. Use it only when a gated commit is genuinely impossible, and expect the `bypass` line in the audit log. It is NOT needed for the docs landing above: decide_scope fast-paths docs, so the gated commit takes seconds. Both historic motivations are obsolete — staged .ri fixtures escalating the gate is answered by splitting fixtures out (task 5536 / the ARTIFACT SCOPE carve-out above), and .git/index.lock contention by a bounded-retry loop.
  - NEVER hand-plant the sentinel (`. hooks/main-gate-lib.sh; main_gate_mark`) to sanction an ungated move. It SUCCEEDS and logs `sanctioned main move`, indistinguishable from a genuinely gated commit — it defeats the audit trail as well as the gate. If you must bypass, use the bypass var, which logs honestly.
- After ANY commit built from a private index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=<scratch>`), the SHARED index is stale relative to the new HEAD for exactly the committed paths: `git status` shows them as staged `D` (deleted) plus untracked, and a sibling session committing from the shared index can sweep those DELETIONS into its own commit. Immediately run `git reset -q -- <those files>` (pathspec-only index sync — no ref move, so it is ENFORCE-safe) and confirm `git status --porcelain -- <files>` is clean.
- NEVER `git checkout -b` in project_root — it moves the running orchestrator's checkout off main.
- NEVER `git update-ref` / `commit-tree` / `reset` plumbing to move main. Under the live `reify.mainGate.enforce=true` these plant no sentinel, so reference-transaction classifies the move UNSANCTIONED and aborts. (A pre-ENFORCE atomic-CAS landing recipe circulated 2026-05-31; it has not worked since ENFORCE went live 2026-06-10. The concurrent-advance problem it addressed is solved safely by `git commit --only <exact paths>`, which builds from a temporary index and is hook-gated.)
- Confirm HEAD == main before committing (the offline lane can leave project_root on another branch).
- pre-commit can exceed a default 2-minute tool timeout; pass timeout >= 300000.
- Expect `.git/index.lock` contention from sibling docs commits — wait for the live holder in a bounded-retry loop; NEVER `rm` the lock.

OBVIATED BY THIS SOP: the branch-landing sidecar-serialization dance. Committing in place makes the on-disk copy and the committed copy identical by construction.

COST EVIDENCE: on 2026-07-25 the resolution-unification and stdlib-namespace PRD .md files landed via merge-queue branches while their capability-manifest .md + .yaml halves were left stranded untracked in project_root — splitting one artifact across two vehicles lost half of it.

reify HARNESS-LAYOUT GATE — the decision rule. CANONICAL INDEX (shrunk from its ~9.5k-char absorbing form 2026-09-08). Fires on a new top-level `crates/<c>/tests/<f>.rs` in one of the 5 consolidatable crates: guards red with unregistered-standalone / unsanctioned-standalone, though the test compiles and passes.

THE RULE: a baseline-manifest row is NOT an option at ANY row count — the "check the crate's COUNT first, then maybe add a row" branch is SUPERSEDED (Leo 2026-07-22, esc-5056-11); the manifest is a shrinking ratchet, not an allow-list. Remedy is consolidation: a `#[path]`-declaring `harness_<sub>.rs` root, or folding into an existing grandfathered file or subsystem harness. LIVE CONTRADICTION: some peers still offer "a row added in the same diff" as a mechanism — that restates the superseded branch (ledger peer, Error B).

PEERS, by subject: guard signatures and preflight abort; move mechanics (`#[path=...] mod` MANDATORY, `#![cfg]` survival, `mod common` -> `use crate::common`); folding into an existing grandfathered file (collision, stale-selector); `--from-git`'s false GREEN pre-commit; kLOC cap rule (a) — the WHOLE COMPILE UNIT (root + module dir + escaping includes charged per including unit), SPLIT not a raised cap; scope and exemptions; census volatility and the `^crates/` anchor; the same-diff baseline-row deletion a leaf owes; the anti-refold ledger.

Accretion warning: append to a peer under this topic or write a new SHORT single-claim peer stamped `harness-layout-gate-decision-rule` — never an unstamped entry, never a regrown concatenation.

INDEX — `pkill -f` / `pgrep -f` SELF-MATCH in reify agent sessions. The Claude Code Bash tool runs your command inside a `bash -c '… eval …'` wrapper whose own command line contains your pattern, so `-f` matching always sees the caller. Two failure modes: KILL — `pkill -f` kills your own shell (exit 144; the rest of a compound command never runs); CHECK — a `pgrep -f` probe or `while`/`until pgrep -f` waiter reports ALIVE forever. Rule: never match processes by a pattern your own command line contains; kill by resolved PID; prefer completion signals (the work's own exit, a log sentinel, an artifact mtime) over process matching. Separate hazard, separate topic: on this shared host `-f` also matches OTHER lanes' identical command lines — see topic process-liveness-shared-host (7664f16b-5f4c-4336-957e-aaccc6cf8d75). Peers (topic pkill-pgrep-self-match): d4b39613-bd62-4ad6-98e1-105cfcca254b KILL mode + PID / TaskStop remedy · 512baf8c-4e84-4fd2-9a29-52a6f2c68ac1 collect PIDs at spawn, kill by PID · 85895ba4-820a-4eca-bb5d-832e40d4a3eb killing a watcher: split pattern, /proc cmdline filter, queue-dir + level scope · 108a8f27-940a-4079-b2aa-bf3c95b639d5 boolean `pgrep -f … && echo ALIVE` false positive · 3475efe0-26e0-4fb8-b6c0-f20e71a5b85c anchor the pattern on the interpreter path · e26679a3-cbc7-4de0-90aa-6adfa2968378 waiter never exits + the `setsid … & echo $!` wrong-PID trap · 3cd67410-e14d-4420-b5ee-fc2c816e34b4 waiter never exits + cross-lane matches · 37bd1911-e2b0-4667-ac9f-33cf51bf59ef CHECK-mode remedies with no PID (bracket trick, `pgrep -x`, logs / mtime). To extend: write a SHORT peer stamped topic=pkill-pgrep-self-match — never append to this index, never write an unstamped entry.

Orchestrator/fused-memory pytest-xdist gotcha (canonical, merges bbe45a4f's 6 prior entries + 6d203bd5 + 0ebfcaa7): orchestrator/pyproject.toml and fused-memory/pyproject.toml hardcode `-n auto --dist loadgroup --max-worker-restart=0` in [tool.pytest.ini_options] addopts. Passing `-p no:xdist` on the CLI to force serial execution FAILS with "unrecognized arguments: -n --dist --max-worker-restart=0" — pytest parses addopts AFTER the plugin is disabled, so xdist's own CLI options are no longer registered to consume those flags.

IMPORTANT nuance (corrects a prior contradiction between two merged entries): BOTH cross-file selection styles can spuriously report "no tests ran" (or "file or directory not found") under `--dist loadgroup`, even though the tests collect fine — this is a pytest-xdist + custom-reporter quirk, not reliably avoided by switching between styles: (a) multiple fully-qualified `path::Class::test` node IDs spanning files, and (b) a cross-file `-k "name_a or name_b"` keyword filter spanning multiple test files. Do NOT treat "switch from node-IDs to -k" or "switch from -k to node-IDs" as a dependable fix — either selection style can fail depending on collection/grouping, and one entry's "use -k instead" previously contradicted another's "use node-ID instead."

The ONE reliably robust workaround is `-n0`, which cleanly overrides addopts' `-n auto` (last `-n` wins) and forces serial execution without touching plugin registration (~1s startup for a single in-process test; xdist still pays ~27-30s worker-pool startup even for one selected test under the default distributed mode — expected overhead, not a hang/regression). Example: `python -m pytest tests/<file>::<Class>::<test> -n0`. Note the Bash tool's cwd can drift between calls — prefix pytest invocations with an explicit `cd <pkg-dir> &&`. Contrast: the escalation/ package has NO forced xdist in its addopts, so targeted runs there are fast and accept `-p no:xdist` / normal flags without issue.

SECOND, DISTINCT `-p no:xdist` failure mode: silent FIXTURE loss (task 3875). The above covers `-p no:xdist` erroring with "unrecognized arguments: -n --dist" when addopts still carries `-n auto`. This is the OTHER case: pairing `-p no:xdist` with `-o addopts=` clears addopts so that error does NOT fire, but unregistering the plugin also removes its FIXTURES. `worker_id` is supplied solely by pytest-xdist, so every test requesting it ERRORs at setup ("fixture 'worker_id' not found") and no assertion body runs. `orchestrator.verify._serial_pytest_str` appends exactly `-p no:xdist -o addopts=` for the offline-deep lane's red-path confirm re-run — that is how 14 fused-memory tests across 5 files were reported "failing" and mis-attributed to an unrelated suspect commit.

FIXED ON MAIN 2026-08-24 for fused-memory — task 3875 landed at main 7169009858 (until then this entry described the remedy only prospectively). `worker_id` IS now defined in the SUBPROJECT test-root conftest, fused-memory/tests/conftest.py (the lane runs `cd fused-memory && pytest tests/`, so rootdir is the subproject and the repo-root conftest.py is never loaded), session-scoped to match xdist's own scope, and delegates to `resolve_xdist_worker_id` in fused-memory/tests/_fm_helpers.py, which calls `xdist.plugin.get_xdist_worker_id` through a FUNCTION-LOCAL import — the xdist MODULE stays importable when only the PLUGIN is unregistered, so delegation works in exactly the broken case and cannot drift from xdist's semantics when xdist is healthy. Regression guard: fused-memory/tests/test_worker_id_fixture.py, whose `test_worker_id_survives_the_lanes_serial_confirm_rerun` spawns a NESTED pytest under the lane's exact `-p no:xdist -o addopts=` flags — an in-process assertion cannot catch this class of bug, because the outer run already holds the fixture the child lacks.

SCOPE OF THAT FIX — fused-memory ONLY. The fixture lives in fused-memory's own test-root conftest, not a shared/repo-root one (the repo-root conftest.py defines no `worker_id`). Any OTHER subproject whose tests request `worker_id` still hits the original silent-fixture-loss failure under `-p no:xdist -o addopts=`. The canonical `-n0` workaround above does NOT hit this failure mode at all, since it leaves plugin registration intact.

THIRD, DISTINCT failure mode: WORKER CRASH UNDER LOAD is a flake, not a test failure (task 4381). A run reports "1 failed" whose ONLY evidence is `worker 'gwN' crashed while running <nodeid>` plus `xdist: worker gwN crashed and worker restarting disabled`, with NO assertion output and NO traceback from the test body — that combination is the tell. `--max-worker-restart=0` in addopts makes a single worker death terminal, and the death is attributed to whichever test that worker happened to be holding, so the named test is a bystander, not the cause. Observed 2026-08-20 on task 4381: orchestrator tests/test_merge_queue_restart_hook.py::test_stop_does_not_preempt_finalizing_head_mid_advance died in a 33-worker run while the live merge queue was concurrently verifying another task; the same file rerun with `-n0` gave 10 passed. Before attributing such a failure to a branch, rerun the file serially with `-n0` — and note this is precisely the case where reaching for `-p no:xdist` instead runs NOTHING at all, which is easily misread as a pass.

CAUTION 3 (added 2026-09-14, reconciliation run b4fd1c79): peer ordinal self-numbering under this topic has drifted and is NOT reliable. At least four peers independently self-label as "the fifth" distinct failure mode while documenting four DIFFERENT things — 2578b8cc (task 4481, esc-4481-6, 2026-09-07), 8c71d002 (task 3561, 2026-09-04), 2df6373e (task 5079, 2026-09-05), and a4bcdff6 (task 4609, 2026-09-14) — because no peer queried current topic membership before numbering itself. True membership as of this note: 13 records tagged `topic: pytest-xdist-serial-override` (confirm via `get_memories_by_metadata`/`count_memories_by_metadata`, never by trusting a peer's own ordinal). Read a peer's CONTENT to learn which distinct failure mode it documents; do not rely on any "fourth"/"fifth"/etc. claim in its text.

ACCRETION: this is the canonical entry for topic `pytest-xdist-serial-override`. Append here, or write a stamped peer under that topic — do not write a new unstamped entry. A same-topic procedural_knowledge write is soft-blocked by add_memory's topic-cluster guard; if your content is genuinely distinct, override with metadata={'allow_near_duplicate': True}.

ADDING A TOOL TO THE reify-debug MCP — CANONICAL (consolidates 9 entries, 2026-05-05..2026-06-09, under curator gate esc-5563-1; addendum folded 2026-08-30, see end). Verified against the tree 2026-07-27. DIFFERENT TOPIC, do not merge: DRIVING the debug MCP is topic=reify-debug-mcp-driving (gate esc-5561-1).

AUTHORITY, USE IT INSTEAD OF TRUSTING THIS PROSE: `gui/src/__tests__/debugParity.test.ts` mechanically extracts the ToolDef names from the Rust source (regex over `ToolDef { name: "..." }`) and checks frontend/Rust parity. It is the executable contract; this entry only orients you. If prose and that test disagree, the test wins.

WHERE THE REGISTRY LIVES — a persistent PRD-level misdirection worth stating first. The registry is `gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs`: `tool_defs() -> Vec<ToolDef>` and `dispatch_tool(state, name, params)`. It is NOT in `gui/src-tauri/src/debug.rs`, despite several PRDs (GR-016 §2.3 inventory row, mesh-morphing.md cross-ref) and task descriptions calling it "the debug.rs registry". `debug.rs` houses the unrelated `DebugBridge` used for frontend-mediated oneshot RPCs. And there is NO `gui/src-tauri/src/debug_bridge.rs` at all, despite some task metadata referencing it (confirmed absent 2026-07-27).

THE RULE: a FRONTEND-MEDIATED tool — one that reads the DOM or Solid stores rather than the OCCT engine — needs only TWO touch points:
1. a `ToolDef` entry in `tool_defs()` (gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs) with name, description and an object-typed JSON input_schema;
2. a handler in the `buildHandlers(ctx)` map in `gui/src/debug/bridge.ts`.
NO new Rust dispatch match-arm is required. `dispatch_tool`'s default arm — `_ => state.debug_bridge.query_frontend(name, params).await` — already forwards any unmatched tool name to the JS bridge. Consequence worth knowing: a bridge-only handler works via `tools/call` without rebuilding the Tauri binary.

THREE EXCEPTIONS THAT DO NEED MORE:
- STATE-BOUND / ENGINE-OR-DISK tools get an explicit Rust arm, via the `run_on_engine` helper: engine_state, mesh_stats, open_file, wait_for_idle, load_fixture, the stateless morph stats.
- IMAGE-RETURNING tools (screenshot, screenshot_window, element_screenshot) must ALSO be listed in `is_image_tool()`, or `tools/call` will not strip the data-URL prefix and emit an MCP image content block.
- FRONTEND STORE FIELDS your handler reads must be added to the `DebugStores` type in `gui/src/debug/types.ts`. That type exposes only a STRUCTURAL SUBSET of the real engineStore — e.g. it lacked compileDiagnostics/tessellationDiagnostics until task 4297. A field missing there is a silent read failure, not a compile error in the Rust half.

TESTS
- Rust-side, for a frontend-mediated tool, just assert the tool_defs schema (object type, required fields) — there is no Rust behaviour to test. Precedents live alongside in debug_server.rs's own test module (tool_defs_includes_set_camera, tool_defs_contains_set_test_mode, tool_defs_includes_screenshot_window, is_image_tool_recognizes_both_screenshot_variants).
- Frontend bridge unit tests go in `gui/src/__tests__/debugBridge.test.tsx` — note the `.TSX` extension. Task metadata `files` lists sometimes say `.ts`, which does not exist.
- JSDOM GOTCHA: jsdom has no layout engine, so `getBoundingClientRect()` returns width 0 under vitest. A handler that needs visibility must use CSS visibility instead — this is why the `ui_outline` handler does.

LINE NUMBERS ROT — cite symbols. The retired entries pinned dispatch_tool's default arm at "~:481"; as of 2026-07-27 it is at :1069, with tool_defs at :35, is_image_tool at :1030, dispatch_tool at :1047 and run_on_engine at :1077. Grep the symbol.

ADDENDUM (2026-08-30, folds 35275359 — this entry's own norm is to extend it rather than write another): adding a ToolDef also reds FOUR drift surfaces beyond the two-touch-point rule above, which must be updated in the SAME commit: (1) the dispatch_tool match arm itself, for a state-bound tool (or confirm the default arm's frontend delegation is what you intend); (2) gui/src/__tests__/debugParity.test.ts — a tool with no same-named buildHandlers() entry in bridge.ts must be listed in PURE_ENGINE_SIDE, and check (e) then requires that entry to actually exhibit the asymmetry; (3) gui/test/visual/assertions.ts KNOWN_DEBUG_TOOL_NAMES, mechanically enforced as a superset of tool_defs() by assertions.test.ts case (a) (task-5934); (4) docs/debug-mcp-contract.md §0. Separately, the tool name must be a literal `ToolDef { name: "..." }` with chars only in [a-z0-9_]: gui/src/__tests__/toolDefNames.ts extracts names via `/ToolDef\s*\{\s*name:\s*"([a-z0-9_]+)"/` and cross-checks the count against raw `ToolDef {` occurrences, so a computed or uppercase/hyphenated name surfaces as a count mismatch rather than being silently dropped.

(Consolidated from 69b7dfd9, 243b6dec, 9f32e820, c315352b, 41f3e4f8, 420be09b, 935ecd70, 58ba125e, and the borderline candidate d3a57bb8 — which DID belong: its registry-file-identity correction is the same "where do I edit" question, and 935ecd70 had independently rediscovered half of it. Nine entries restating one two-step rule over five weeks; the differentiating content was entirely in the exceptions and the file-identity corrections, all preserved above. If you rediscover this, extend this entry or the parity test — do not write a tenth.)

reify: the `tracing` callsite-Interest cache-poisoning gotcha, and the TWO legitimate remedies. CANONICAL (merges 2200d20e + 524933e4 + 2eda458f, curator gate esc-5626-1, verified against the tree 2026-07-27; further merged 2026-08-13 by recon Stage 1 memory_consolidator with 4a3f8f0c [mechanism precision] and 687622db [task 6273 correction] and a347f32b [counter type note] — see UPDATE below; UPDATE section requalified 2026-08-13 by recon Stage 1 memory_consolidator, run 4b693a7d-2e7e-46c4-9b42-5c1b1b4166d0, after re-verification against the tree — see REMEDIATION note at end).

ROOT CAUSE: in Rust `tracing`, callsite `Interest` is cached PROCESS-GLOBALLY, but `tracing::subscriber::with_default` is THREAD-LOCAL. A unit test that installs a capturing subscriber via `with_default` and asserts a `tracing::debug!`/`info!`/`warn!` event fired will FLAKE if any sibling test in the same test binary reaches that same callsite FIRST with no subscriber installed. MEASURED (reify-eval, task 5075): 6 of 12 runs failed; two consecutive identical `cargo test` invocations gave opposite results; passes in isolation with `-- --exact`. Applies to reify's widespread `CapturingSubscriberBuilder`/`CountingSubscriberBuilder`/`warn_counting_subscriber` + `with_default` idiom (~20+ files across reify-eval, reify-compiler, reify-kernel-{occt,gmsh,manifold}, reify-constraints, reify-lsp, reify-solver-elastic, reify-mesh-morph).

MECHANISM (verified line-by-line against the pinned tracing-core 0.1.36): `callsite::DefaultCallsite::register` (callsite.rs:308) caches a callsite's `Interest` on its FIRST hit via `Dispatchers::rebuilder()`. `rebuilder()` returns `Rebuilder::JustOne` whenever `has_just_one == true` (the normal state in a test binary — `register_dispatch` stores `dispatchers.len() <= 1` after pruning dead weak refs), and `JustOne::for_each` consults ONLY the REGISTERING THREAD's `dispatcher::get_default()`. A subscriber-less sibling libtest thread resolves that to `NoSubscriber` -> `Interest::never()` (subscriber.rs:676), and the callsite is then elided at the macro gate for EVERY thread thereafter. With >=2 live dispatchers the rebuilder ANDs them (`Interest::and`, subscriber.rs:658), which is why intermittency needs exactly `has_just_one == true`. Two corrected misconceptions: (a) it is NOT `set_global_default` alone that rebuilds the cache — `Dispatch::new` does (dispatcher.rs:479, calls `callsite::register_dispatch`), and `set_global_default`/`set_default`/`with_default` all construct a `Dispatch`, so all three trigger a rebuild; (b) a rebuild only fixes ALREADY-registered callsites, never one whose first hit is still ahead. Note: libtest sorts test names alphabetically, so modules sorting before the first priming module (e.g. `claude_bridge_tests`/`diff_tests` vs `engine_tests` in reify-gui) were the ones that flaked.

REMEDY 1 — MECHANICAL, when the tracing event genuinely IS the contract under test: call `reify_test_support::prime_tracing_callsite_cache()` before the event's first hit. It installs a process-global default `Priming` subscriber whose `register_callsite` returns `Interest::sometimes()`, disabling the static never-cache so `enabled()` is consulted per-event; it also repairs callsites already poisoned by an earlier sibling. This explicit call is REQUIRED at all ~40 existing call sites — see UPDATE below for status of a proposed automatic variant.
